steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC) was a rebellion of Greek city-states in Asia Minor against Persian rule | Key Fact: Aristagoras, tyrant of Miletus, initiated the revolt after a failed attack on Naxos left him fearing Persian punishment | Key Fact: Athens sent 20 ships and Eretria sent 5 to support the Ionians — this enraged King Darius | Key Fact: The burning of Sardis (498 BC) was the revolt's greatest success but provoked a devastating Persian response

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from the ionian revolt (499-494 bc), and one past-paper question.
